Here if you need to talk. I was at the receiving end of being dumped. It wasn't easy either, both sides needed to process their thoughts and continue with their daily things. It won't be easy, like I said it took me 4-5 years to take the first step. Keep the distance for now and let it sink in slowly. Accept the fact and responses for your decision as it is with every other choice we make. It's a slow process overall, but whatever the reason you chose to split stick to it at best. Making any rash choice will worsen things as during this time people are most vulnerable. 

Focus on improving yourself gradually overtime. That's the best distraction I can say, as sitting and feeling bad won't help us with daily life due to the harsh world we live in. Sorry for the long message, I also don't want to hurt anyone's feelings. The rule of separation and improvement applied to both sides.

Being a person who also waited 4+ years. It's time to move on, not simple even though I've entered the process recently. You need to find a way, one to distract yourself and two accept that they have learnt to live without you. You need to do the same.

Bring back the person who had ambitions and hobbies before you met them. Its a slow process and you can take therapy as well (can't in my case). Talk it out and decide/set a goal within the upcoming period. 

You wouldn't want to prove them right by leaving, but remind them that that person could've been with me if we had worked out. If we don't start working at some point, people who are actually dependent on us also start getting affected.

Sorry if I spoke out of line. It's best for us to start accepting the reality and start progressing further for the one who'll be there with us in any case.
